utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We both speak the same language. I'd like to ask you to wait, following the end of my questions, before providing your answers. And when answering, try to do your utmost so as to enable everyone working on this case to do their work in a quality way and so that we can move along speedily. Mr. Misic, for the needs of the transcript, could you please give us your personal information.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: My name is Stojan Misic. Born on the 3rd of April, 1949, in the village of Prevalac, the municipality of Vranje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you retire, Mr. Misic?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I retired in late 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I have a law degree, and I passed the bar exam.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In brief, can you give us an overview of your professional career?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: At the law school in Belgrade, I graduated in 1973. I had my internship with the county court in Vranje where I also passed the bar exam in 1976. In 1977, I became employed with the joint Secretariat of the Interior in Leskovac. That secretariat covered the area of Leskovac. I was appointed assistant secretary of the joint secretariat for combatting crime. I worked there until 1981 when I was appointed chief of secretariat in Vranje. I remained in that position until 1986. That year, I was assigned to the Republican Secretariat of the Interior answerable -- which later on became the Ministry of the Interior. My position was that of chief of administration for combatting crime. I remained in that position until 1990. In 1990/1991, I was appointed by the government to be the assistant minister. I remained in that position until 2002 [as interpreted]. Given that a number of governments changed during that period of time, I was appointed on a number of occasions to be assistant minister. Until 1997, I was assistant minister in charge of combatting crime and crime police. As of 1997, I was assistant minister in charge of alien affairs, travel documents, as well as fire-fighting and communications. I became major-general in 1996 in March. In 2000, in July, I was promoted to the rank lieutenant-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the needs of the transcript, in line 25, it is stated that you were assistant minister until 2002?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: No, that was until 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P263. Your Honours, before moving to the document, could we please be allowed to provide the hard copies of all documents we intend to use to the witness in order to move speedily along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another thing, Your Honour, could we go into private session for just a moment. I forgot one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Misic, please open your binder. As you can see, each document has a tab starting with the number 1 on. I'll tell you precisely which tab you will require and, of course, we'll start with tab 1. This is a dispatch of the minister of the interior, Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic, dated 4 June 1997. Briefly, can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: This dispatch bears the date of the 4th of June, 1997. It was sent from the Ministry of the Interior. In the signature block we see that the name of the minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, appears. He informed all organisational units at the seat of the ministry, both the public and state security sectors, as well as all organisational units in the area of the Republic of Serbia and all Secretariats of Internal Affairs, as well as the MUP staff and border police stations, the police academy, college of Internal Affairs, the secondary school of Internal Affairs, and the security institute. He informs them that he had issued a decision by virtue of which he appointed General Vlastimir Djordjevic, assistant minister, as of June 1, 1997, to the position of the chief of the public security sector. Your Honours, perhaps you could advise me of my speed. Am I speaking too slowly or too fast?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You seem to be doing well at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. He also informed all of the organisational units that at a session of the Serbian government which was held on the same day, Major-General Petar Zekovic and Major-General Obrad Stevanovic were appointed assistant ministers. My name does not appear here because, as I've already explained, I was appointed assistant minister back in 1991. We can also see that the minister informs the addressees of the tasks he had assigned to the aforementioned assistant ministers. Among other things, he states that Major-General Stojan Misic was in charge of the administration for foreigners, administrative and legal affairs, fire prevention police, and communication affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: For the needs of the transcript, could you please repeat what you said concerning Vlastimir Djordjevic. What position was he appointed to as of June 1?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-General Vlastimir Djordjevic was appointed assistant minister as well as acting chief of the public security sector. It was the first time in my year long career in the police that we had an acting chief of the public security sector. Such a situation did not occur any time after that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had the word "acting" missing from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We can see by way of dispatch, this dispatch, the minister assigned domains or remits to each of the assistant ministers. Can you tell us what affairs were the assistant ministers in charge of?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Assistant ministers are professionals assisting the work of the minister of the interior. I.e., they are each assigned different areas of responsibility; they are in charge of monitoring those areas; and of putting forth proposals in order to deal with certain problems by way of minister's decisions. They put these proposals to the minister. And in cases in which he accepts their proposals, they are then in turn tasked with implementing them through the various organisational units. It is for that reason that they forward instructional dispatches, monitor the implementation of tasks, and inform the minister of it. Therefore, assistant ministers do not have their individual original authority to issue any or -- issue any measures to the organisational units. This can only be done by the minister himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can assistant ministers act on the minister's orders in order to undertake certain measures?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Assistant ministers in any case act on the minister's orders or instructions in order to undertake specific measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see in this dispatch that the minister allocated the work lines to the deputy ministers [as interpreted]. Under what type of tasks do these professional lines of work fall in view of the classification of internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In view of the internal structure of the MUP and in view of the tasks the ministry carries out, we have here practically assistant ministers who are only in charge of public security tasks. We have two departments in the ministry: the state security department that deals with the security issues concerning the republic and state affair; and then we have the public security sector that deals with public security. So here we see assistant ministers who were covering different areas in the public security section.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 4, in my question, it is erroneously written "deputy minister," it should state "assistant minister." This is on page 6, actually, line 4. Page 24 [as interpreted], line 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, and this relationship among the assistant ministers, what was that like?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The assistant minister has their own immediate superior, that is, the minister. He is the superior officer to all assistant ministers. But they are equal. They cannot issue assignments to each other. Once they do receive an assignment from the minister, they are responsible for the execution of those assignments to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 7, line 3, again, it's stated again "deputy minister" instead of "assistant minister."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when we are here dealing with these problems, we are having problems with the transcript, what is the difference, Mr. Misic, between the deputy minister and the assistant minister for Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The deputy minister and assistant minister are appointed by the government. There is a major difference in their powers. When we are talking about the deputy minister, his original powers are such that if the minister is absent, he can take all the measures and actions that are in the jurisdiction of the minister of the MUP. He can handle all of these jobs. As far as assistant ministers are concerned, they do not have those same powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, this dispatch that we have in front of us, number 263, who has been given certain professional sectors to deal with and which are those posts?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question. You are talking about this dispatch that we have in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Other than what I have already said about the tasks that I was in charge with --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Misic, let's just see which persons were carrying out which tasks.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: These people were carrying out the function of assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic was minister of Internal Affairs, was anyone the deputy minister? Was such a post assigned by the government?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: During the tenure of Vlajko Stojiljkovic, there was no deputy minister. We had a deputy minister with the previous minister, Mr. Sokolovic; and there was a deputy minister before him when Minister Bogdanovic was in office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, during 1998 and 1999, what were the duties of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia carries out the duties as laid down by law for a state organ of that type. They deal with the protection and security that pertains to the republic. They carry out duties of protecting the lives and the property of citizens, and they take care of their safety. Then they maintain public law and order. They also have crime fighting functions, as well as processing and prosecuting and finding the perpetrators of criminal acts. They also deal with traffic security issues, border control, and checks of foreigners and aliens. There is also the fire-fighting police force. There are also internal administrative affairs such as the issuance of personal ID cards, certificates of citizenship, issuance of passports, and so on and so forth. These duties are distributed or divided between state security, which is protection of the republic, and public security, which comprise all the other jobs that I have just listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us, in 1988 [as interpreted] and 1999, who was at the head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In 1999 and 1998, the head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs was the minister, Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what were the minister's tasks and duties pursuant to the regulations and the laws of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The minister was at the head of the ministry pursuant to the provisions of the law. The minister represented the Ministry of Internal Affairs. He organised an efficient and responsible execution of Internal Affairs tasks, and he decided on the duties and the responsibilities and the rights of the employees of the MUP. He was responsible for his work and the work of the ministry as a whole. Upon the request -- actually, the minister was elected and dismissed by the National Assembly upon the request of the National Assembly or the president of the republic. The minister was obliged to submit reports about the security situation in the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what were the powers of the minister of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: He was authorised to set the manner in which work and duties would be executed, and pursuant to that, he would issue the appropriate instructions on the execution of tasks in the sphere of Internal Affairs. He was also authorised to issue directives and regulations, administrative guide-lines, and make decisions on specific matters in his jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how were the duties of the MUP actually carried out in terms of organisation?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Oh, all right, in terms of organisation. I emphasised earlier that the Ministry of Internal Affairs had two departments: the public security department and the state security department. We also had organisational units that were outside of those two departments, meaning schools, secondary school, higher school, the security institute, and we also had a department for legal and general affairs. As for public security, these -- we mentioned earlier what the duties of that department were. As far as the organisational structure is concerned, if I may be permitted to speak about that, the public security department consisted of organisational units at the headquarters of the public security department, and it also had organisational units which were outside of the headquarters. These were territorial organisational units throughout the entire territory of the republic, meaning that the entire republic was covered by a network of basic organisational units. As far as organisational units at the seat were concerned, the minister decided that these would be referred to as administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just interrupt you. Can we look at Exhibit P357.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is in tab 2 in your binder, sir. And while we are waiting to see this document on the screen, would you just kindly tell us, General, sir, who determined the scope of activity of organisational units, their respective areas and seats?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Their sphere of activity would be determined by the minister of Internal Affairs by the adoption of appropriate regulations which would be called the rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have these rules on the internal organisation of these units here in front of us. Can you please tell us, this document regulates the organisation of which sector of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: This document regulates only the public security department, and in the document itself, it is stated that a special set of rules will be adopted regulating the department of state security, primarily because of the confidential nature of that department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 9 of the English version and page 11 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your copy, sir, this is page 9 of the rules.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Excuse me just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page. Actually, at the top of the page you will see that it is -- that's where the page number is. Now, let's look at Article 13. Can you please tell us what types of organisational units are these?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Just like I said before, they were organisational units established at the seat of the ministry, and they are mentioned on page 9. If needed, I can say that these are the crime police administration, police administration --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There's no need. We can see that ourselves.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: All right. We have 11 administrations, and they were all located at the seat of the ministry, and they covered certain areas of activity. In order to be able to follow more easily how matters proceeded, we referred to these administrations as professional lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was the organisational structure of the administrations at the seat of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Their organisation at the seat of the ministry was such that there were sections. Then after that we had divisions as organisational units within the administration. And then at the end, of course, we had Working Groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us what were the assignments of the administrations within the seat of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Their duties, first of all, were to direct, co-ordinate, and have an overview the work of their units in the whole territory of the republic as professional lines of work. They would issue instructions, directions, rules of conduct in order to provide uniform methods and advance the work of organisational units in the territory of the whole Republic, that is to say, secretariats and their lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you please tell us what were the territorial organisational units outside of the seat of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Territorial organisational units outside of the ministry were secretariats for Internal Affairs as the main basic territorial organisational units of the ministry, and they each covered an area. And overall they covered the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia. Besides that, the secretariats also covered, and I'm speaking generally, certain regions as administrative units, although there were some differences there. In other municipalities outside of the secretariat seat, there were organisational units such as the Departments of Internal Affairs or police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come to that. Just -- can you please tell us if you recall how many SUPs there were in the territory of the Republic of Serbia in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I remember that. I did this kind of work for many years. There were 33 secretariats on the territory of the whole republic. There were seven secretariats in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina, and also seven secretariats in the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija, and there were 19 secretariats which covered the rest of the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us something about the internal organisation of the secretariat for Internal Affairs, please?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The Secretariats of Internal Affairs also had organisational units at the seat of the secretariat and organisational units outside of the secretariat seat. The organisational units at the seat of the SUP as a rule were departments; and in smaller municipalities, smaller secretariats, they had divisions; and then within those we had groups which were grouped by the type of assignment. So that was practically the type of organisation which corresponded to the organisation at the seat of the ministry according to the lines of activity, but at the ministry we had 11 such professional lines, and at the secretariats we had 8 such lines, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What tasks did the SUPs have?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I omitted something. I needed to say that the SUP in Belgrade was also organised in a way that at the seat of the SUP in Belgrade we had administrations as organisational units which corresponded to the organisational units at the seat of the ministry. It was done this way because the secretariat in Belgrade was the largest secretariat covering the most territory, and it had the most complex issues to deal with, as well as the greatest number of crimes and perpetrators. That is why its organisational structure had to be more developed than was the case with the other secretariats. We also omitted to say what organisational units there existed outside the secretariat seat. Those were the so-called OUPs, or departments of Internal Affairs, as well as police stations. Police stations were established in those municipalities which had small populations and fewer problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was what were the tasks of the SUPs?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The Secretariats of Internal Affairs had all tasks within the remit of the ministry concerning Internal Affairs to deal with in the seat of the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about OUPs and police stations?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Internal Affairs departments and police stations dealt directly with all Internal Affairs tasks in their respective municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was at the helm of the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The public security sector was headed by the chief of that sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1998 and 1999 who was the chief of the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Chief of the public security sector in those two years was Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was at the helm of the administrations in the seat of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Those administrations were headed by chiefs of administrations who were in charge of the administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was at the head of SUPs and OUPs?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: At the helm of the SUPs and OUPs, there were chiefs of secretariats and chiefs of OUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, who appointed those in charge of the public security sector, starting with the chief of the sector and going down to chiefs of administrations and chiefs of the SUPs and OUPs?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The people you just referred to were appointed by the minister because he was the only one who had the original power to appoint key officials, i.e., those in charge of the organisational units in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how the minister headed the ministry?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In principle I had in mind the minister as an institution.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Given my large experience, my rich experience, because I worked with a number of different ministers, it all depended on the type and method of work of each individual minister. Therefore, we had different management styles represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what sort of management styles existed?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: First of all, we had minister's collegiums, that was one method of work. We also had sessions, periodical sessions, attended by all leading personnel from all the organisations. Such sessions and meetings were held periodically, quarterly. So within any given year, as a rule, we had four or even more sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain the way the MUP was managed when Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic was minister?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic used to be the chief of the secretariat of internal affairs in Pozarevac. He was very confident in his belief that he was very familiar with the overall domain of public security. In the performance of his duties, he occasionally assumed the authority of even those around him. He frequently summoned chiefs of administrations and even some junior officials without the knowledge of the chiefs of sectors or assistant ministers in charge of certain areas issuing them tasks. Later on he would not inform us, undermining our authority. He also sent certain assistant ministers to replace certain officials without previously informing sector chiefs or assistant ministers. We were in an uneasy situation therefore. By introducing this type of management, hierarchical relationships that used to exist in the ministry was undermined, including the entire subordination system.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you provide a specific example to illustrate what you've just said?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I recall a case in which the chief of the SUP in Vranje came to Belgrade to deal with certain issues that had to do with finances and materiel. First he went to see the chief of sector, and he also came to see me for consultations. After that, he went back to Vranje. In the course of that evening, he called me stating that he was replaced, removed from his position. And he insisted that I told him why he was replaced and why I did not advise him of that previously. I told him I had no knowledge of that whatsoever, and I called Mr. Djordjevic to check with him whether he was informed of that. He was as surprised as I was, stating that he had no idea. In the meantime, the assistant public security sector chief Dragisa was sent to the field and he removed the SUP of Vranje chief. There were also situations in which he issued specific tasks circumventing sector chiefs or assistant ministers in charge of certain areas such as the area of combatting crime. It was in that area in particular where he issued tasks in this direct way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D434.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 3. We will see and excerpt from a meeting of the minister and the secretariat chiefs held on the 16th of September [as interpreted], 1999, in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything about such meetings as a method of work and in particular this meeting, the summary of which we can see here?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: This was one of the ways of managing and directing the entire Ministry of Internal Affairs by way of periodical meetings. We can see that this meeting was held on the 16th of October, 1998. The agenda included items pertaining to the analysis of work conducted between January and September 1998. There's also a number of specific tasks mentioned therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there. Who attended this meeting, people from which sector?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: It was attended by members of the public security sector. At the meeting, the security situation was discussed in terms of public security as we have just discussed a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So as -- so that the Chamber and the Prosecution could follow, could we please move to page 2 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, who attended this meeting of the 16th of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by the minister, Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic, as well as assistant ministers Radomir Markovic and Petar Zekovic. Next, there were assistant chiefs of the public security sector, Dragisa Dinic and Marinko Kresoja. I chaired the meeting, and it was attended by all chiefs of all administrations at the seat of the ministry as well as by the chiefs of Secretariats of Internal Affairs in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see from the minutes that the chiefs of administration submitted their reports on the results of their work for the first nine months of year and that the minister provided feedback by way of an assessment of their work. In that period, that is to say after the first nine months of 1998, what was the most important security-related task in the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The most important security-related task at the time was the situation in Kosovo and Metohija. There were terrorist activities underway, and one of the priorities in any case was to address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you analyse the anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija during that meeting in the aforementioned period?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: We did not analyse any anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija at the meeting. Only the minister provided a general assessment stating that the tasks in that domain were executed well in the fight against terrorism. Apart from his contribution, there were no other analyses or contributions by any chiefs of secretariats or chiefs of administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next please have page 6 in the English and your page 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, you said page 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, could you comment on paragraphs 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: These are mostly statistics. Mention is made of the measures undertaken against the perpetrators of crimes, as well as what measures were taken in terms of detaining and bringing in persons. That was the statistical data provided for the most part. Next --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 9 in the B/C/S and 10 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have you found page 9?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we have your comments on paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we are talking about page 10 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have it. The paragraph starting with the words "Over the past nine months ..." Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: This paragraph indicates that in the previous nine months joint services were engaged primarily in equipping Special Police Units for special security tasks in the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija. Both at the meeting of the collegium and at this meeting, they put forth their needs and requirements in terms of the procurement of vehicles, explosives, equipment for night vision, and such-like. The proposal made, in terms of logistics, was to take appropriate measures. At this meeting they reported on what they had done over the previous nine months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Misic, General, sir, at such meetings up until the end of 1998 and then up until the end of 1999, did you receive reports and consider matters related to anti-terrorist activities, i.e., prevention of terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1998 and 1999, we did not receive any plans for organising anti-terrorist activities or reports on the implementation of any such plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was charged with these issues within the Ministry of the Interior in the Republic of Serbia in the course of 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999, as far as anti-terrorist activities are concerned, it was the staff for combatting terrorism set up by the minister of the interior on the 16th of June, 1998, that dealt with these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how did you receive information, if any, on the security situation in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: We did not receive reports, but we did receive daily overviews of events from the staff for the prevention of terrorism whereby we were informed about terrorist attacks and provocative incidents and the consequences thereof. This was a way of keeping us informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, collegium, can you explain how it worked within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: As I've already pointed out, the collegium was one of the ways in which the ministry was run. As far as the form and substance are concerned, it depended on the incumbent minister and how he handled matters. I had occasion to attend the collegium of Minister Sokolovic, Zoran Sokolovic, who was minister before Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic. It was a minister's collegium which was attended by chiefs of the service of public security, chief of the state security service, and assistant ministers. I was assistant minister at the time. In principle, these meetings discussed the security situation in the republic. These matters were discussed with a view to improving the work of the ministry. At the close of the meeting, conclusions were adopted, which chiefs of the various sectors, both the state security and public security, were duty-bound to implement. The chiefs of these departments or sectors had their own collegiums; for instance, public security would have its collegium where chiefs of administrations would report on their activity and propose measures, and the chief of the sector would issue directions as to what the focal points and priorities would be for the forthcoming period. Minutes were made of such meetings as well. When it came to the collegium held by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic, the situation was somewhat different. It was in essence a collegium of public security chaired by the minister. Of course, it was the minister's collegium. The collegium was attended by the assistant ministers; minister himself; chief of the public security sector; I have already mentioned assistant ministers, we know who those were; then chiefs of all administrations as well. The sector chief would pass the floor to the minister who would in turn seek from the chiefs of administrations to come out with an analysis of their respective activities. They reported on the results achieved and problems encountered. At the end, assistant ministers and the sector chief would, if they had any important issues to raise, do so. And the minister of the interior, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, would issue conclusions along each of the lines of duty whilst going into such detail as was not really appropriate for the level of a minister. Based on such conclusions, minutes were drafted. It was Mr. Slobodan Krstic who made notes; he was the chief of the analysis department who would make note of the meeting and produce minutes, and they would be sent to all the attendees. And then at the following collegium meeting an analysis would be made of the achievements and activities done to implement minister’s orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up D108.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will find that document behind tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It's not D108, it's D208.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You've just explained to us what Vlajko Stojiljkovic's collegium was like. What we'd like to know is did anyone from the state security sector attend the collegium chaired by the minister?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: As I said before, all the individuals present at this meeting were representatives of public security. In other words, we did not have either the chief or the deputy chief of the state security sector there, we had those who were in charge of the public security sector. Now, when -- during Mr. Sokolovic's term of office there, representatives of the state security sector were present at these meetings at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have D208 before us which is the decision to set up the collegium of the minister of interior dated the 4th of December, 1998. Can you tell us anything more about this decision and the way in which matters were handled by way of this collegium once the decision was issued?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see that the minister issued the decision on the 4th of December, 1998, whereby the collegium of the minister of the interior was set up. Let me note that the state security sector chief was Mr. Jovica Stanisic who did not attend minister's collegiums. Since he was replaced by Mr. Radomir Markovic as chief of public security sector in the month of November, it seems that conditions were in place for one such collegium to be set up. In addition to the chief of the public security sector, also the chief of the state security sector was to be present, as well as his assistant. Another assistant minister, in fact, Mr. Nikola Curcic who was otherwise a director of the security institute. In addition to them, as we can see here, there were also assistant ministers from public security present at this meeting, as well as Dragisa Dinic who was assistant chief of the public security sector. Dragan Ilic, chief of the crime police administration. A moment ago we said that once Mr. Radomir Markovic left and he was in charge of that field, the minister did not appoint anyone else to cover that line of duty. And last but not least, we have Mr. Branko Djuric who was the chief of the Secretariat of the Interior in Belgrade. Furthermore, the decision also indicates that Minister’s Head of Office, Captain Danilo Pantovic, and Colonel Slobodan Krstic, who was chief of the analysis administration, also took part at the meeting of the collegium. And the last person, chief of the analysis department, also handled minutes. In addition to this, it is stated that the collegium meetings could occasionally be attended by any of the other senior staff pursuant to an appropriate minister's decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what the minister's collegium actually looked like and how it worked once this 4 December 1998 decision was issued?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, once the decision was issued, the work of the collegium, in fact, continued as before. At the collegium meeting, the minister asked reports to be submitted by chiefs of administrations. They did so. They also proposed various measures. Then assistant ministers and the sector chief would also take the floor. And at the end the minister would issue conclusions. The only difference lay in the fact that the minister himself would either at the beginning or at the end of the meeting, it depended, a brief overview of the security situation in the Republic of Serbia with particular emphasis on the territory of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija. Later on, a similar overview, only from the perspective of the state security sector, would be given by the state security sector chief. There was no difference in any other aspect, and it was for the most part public security matters that were discussed at this -- at such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that chiefs of administrations attended these meetings, but can you tell us which particular sector these administrations belonged to?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, you see that it is stated here that the collegium is composed of nine members in actual fact. However, the collegium never met in this particular composition. Rather, the previous practice was adhered to whereby all chiefs of administrations would attend, and I mean administrations of the public security sector. Then there would also be -- or, rather, chiefs of administrations of the state security sector never attended these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This way of proceeding at the collegium of the minister following the 4th of December, 1998, did it prevail up until the end of the war in 1999?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The way in which the collegium worked did not change either in 1998 or in 1999. It was public security affairs that were discussed at these collegium meetings at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At collegium meetings held in 1998 and 1999, did you discuss the planning and directing of anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija as well as reports on anti-terrorist activities that had been planned and implemented?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, at the meetings of the minister's collegium, we never discussed planning and implementing anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo, nor did we receive reports on the implementation of these plans. What we practically discussed at collegium meetings were proposals received from administrations, notably police administration and common affairs administration, about the needs that the staff had in terms of logistics. Were these perhaps technical or material issues, issues of equipment, et cetera, the minister would issue decisions aimed at fulfilling these needs. Now, as for the planning and implementing of anti-terrorist activities or a discussion of reports about such plans, this was not something that was discussed at the meetings of the collegium. Rather, the minister would at the start of such meetings give an overview of the security situation in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, sir, can you briefly tell us what the political and security situation was in mid-1998 in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The security situation in Kosovo and Metohija in mid-1998 was extremely complex and difficult. This because there was a large part of the territory under the control of a terrorist organisation. Roads were blocked. There were relentless attacks on the police and the army. Police and army facilities were under attack as well. There were instances of kidnapping, murders of Serbian -- of the Serbian population, as well as of the Albanians who were loyal to the Serbian state. In other words, the situation was very complex and very difficult in mid-1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to move to a different topic, so I suggest that we take our break a bit early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now. We will resume at ten past 4.00. A Court Officer will assist you during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I indicate for your planning, Mr. Djurdjic, that we will need to adjourn a little earlier than usual, between 5.20 and 5.25. So at a convenient time in that area, we'll adjourn for the second break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It's possible that by that time I may even complete my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are full of encouragement, Mr. Djurdjic. That's very good news. We will see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. Mr. Djurdjic will continue his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just a small digression. D208 is no longer on our screens. Perhaps we could get it back. I have just noticed something, so I would kindly ask to see page 2 in both versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, you can also turn to page 2 of the document that you have in front of you, the decision of the minister. Can you please tell us whether there is an attachment for this decision.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I don't see anything like an attachment on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 3, the following page in both versions. Just one moment so that we can see the relevant page in the English as well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, let me ask you this, this list of collegium participants, is that an integral part of the decision that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't be an integral part because this is not indicated in the actual decision. That's one thing. The other thing is that this is probably some kind of attachment, a kind of auxiliary list, and I don't know who drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to the next page in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you can do the same thing, General. So I'm putting the same question again. Is this list and this page an integral part of the decision that we were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In my view it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to ask you this. We see a whole list of names here, and then under number 8 there is a name of Miodrag Zavisic. Did you ever see him in a collegium meeting?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Zavisic was a chief of the secretariat in Novi Sad. I never used to see him at sessions of the collegium, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can now take this document from -- off the screen. We don't need it anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Before the break you informed us about the political security situation in mid-1998. So my question to you would be if, and if so, which measures did the Ministry of Internal Affairs undertake in view of the political security situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: We had several collegium meetings where we analysed the overall security situation and sought adequate solutions. On one occasion, the minister stated at the collegium, that in view of the overall complex security situation, he formed a staff of the ministry for anti-terrorist activities. At that point in time we, or I at least, didn't know that such a decision would be made. He said that in view of the serious situation, it was necessary to unify all the ministry capacities, the state and the public security, in order to be able to deal more effectively with the problem of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have the opportunity to familiarise yourself with this decision by Minister Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have the opportunity to do that a few days afterwards. I and some other assistants looked at this decision at the minister's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the minister tell you before you saw the decision about the kind of staff this would be and the sort of assignments that it would be given?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that a staff was formed for anti-terrorist actions, that the staff was organised in such a way that the staff members, the personnel, were both from the state and public security administrations, that Mr. Sreten Lukic, General Lukic, was at the head of the staff, that his deputy was David Gajic, and that the commanders of the units from the - of the JSO and the anti-terrorist unit were also commanders and part of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D57 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This would be tab 5 in your binder, sir. This is a decision on the forming of the staff of the Ministry for the prevention of terrorism of the 16th of June, 1998. The decision is issued by Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is P57. That's the exhibit. Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, is this the decision that you were informed about by the minister later?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the decision on the establishing of a ministry staff for the suppression of terrorism, dated the 16th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 2 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, were you familiar with the extended composition of the staff at the time the minister informed you about this, about the forming of the staff?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that the expanded composition of the staff would include all the chiefs of the SUPs and the chiefs of the state security centres in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and that members of the staff would comprise the extended staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us who was authorised to establish a staff that would include members of the public and security administrations and would be able to issue the staff with assignments?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: This kind of staff which included members of the state and public security administrations could only be formed by the minister of internal affairs. He was the chief of the organ, the senior officer of the organ. The chief of public security or the chief of state security could not form a staff which would include personnel from both these departments. Cadres from the state security department could not lead or issue assignments to members of the public security sector or vice-versa. Only the minister would be able to form a staff that would include both personnel from the public security department and the state security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The transcript says "centres," public security centres, were you thinking about the administrations?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I was talking about the public security department and the state security department and about CRDB - the centres of the state security department – as well as the secretariats, chiefs of the Secretariats for Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, sir, what was the assignment issued to the staff by the minister?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The minister tasked the staff with planning, organising, and managing the work and engagement of the organisational units of the ministry as well as the deployed units and attached units working on the suppression of terrorist activity in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to clarify for us a little bit paragraph 2 under Roman II of this decision?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: As you can see, the organisational units of the ministry actually are the 19 secretariats, first of all, as well as the deployed units and attached units. And we said earlier these were PJP units of the police and SAJ units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, sir, I'm interested in paragraph 2 under section Roman II, can you please clarify that for us?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Oh, all right. I apologise. As we can see here, they are to plan, organise, and control the work and engagement of organisational units of the ministry and also sent an attached units [as interpreted] in suppressing terrorism in the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija. And we have here, actually, tasks which are closely related with the terrorist actions such as smuggling of weapons and ammunition and explosive devices, the trafficking and smuggling of drugs, illegal crossing of state borders by groups or individuals, and so on and so forth. These are all tasks practically requiring the staff to do the planning, organising, direction and coordination of the work of organisational units. So in that sense we have a lower level directive than the one in the previous paragraph because there it says that they are to plan, organise, and control the work and engagement of organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, what were the organisational units located in Kosovo from June 1998 until the end of the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: From what I know, they were the PJP Units of the police in Kosovo, the SAJ Unit of the police, as well as the state security's unit for special operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment item 3, Roman III, of this decision?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: That deals with the fact that the head of the staff shall report to the minister about his own actions, actions of the staff, and the aspects of the security situation under the remit of the staff, and also about informing the minister about security-related developments, measures taken, and the effects of those measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You, as assistant minister, receive reports about the -- did you receive reports about the work of the staff, and were you invited to attend the collegium meetings, and were you informed about the work of the organs formed by the minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I never received any reports about the work of the staff, nor did I see any reports about the work of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And at these collegiums, or in some other way, were you informed about the planning and the conduct of anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999, we never discussed planning and the conduct of anti-terrorist activities at the collegium sessions, nor did we receive any reports about the implemented activities. I said that we usually would discuss matters that one would refer to logistical support which means that we would have requests from the police administration or general affairs administration to provide certain items, and the minister would instruct that these items be provided. We never discussed any other plans or reports other than this. The collegiums also dealt with the relief of units so that the police administration would also propose which units of the PJP would need to be relieved, and the minister would make appropriate decisions on the engagement of such units at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at paragraph Roman V of the decision, and could you give us your comments on it.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: As far as paragraph 5 about the appointment of members of the ministry to the staff, this was something that was done on the basis of Article 72 of the Law on Internal Affairs. This was actually done by the minister, and then pursuant to approval of the minister this was also something that was done by the chief of the public security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since we have a decision assigning persons who were members of the -- to membership in the staff, why would you then also need to have this decision pursuant to Article 72 as well?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: This would be the original decision of the minister on appointment of staff members, and then you would need to adopt the accompanying decision for purposes of proper employment procedures. And that is why, pursuant to minister’s authorisation, a decision would be issued on sending someone to the Staff in order to regulate the necessary employment and legal issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we look at D284 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 6. Witness, before we move on to the document before us, I wanted to ask you this: By a decision on the creation of the staff to combat terrorism dated the 16th of June, 1998, issued by Mr. Stojiljkovic, what was the procedure envisaged for reporting and the responsibility of those in charge of the staff?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Reporting went directly to the minister about all anti-terrorist operations and activities. Such reports had to be sent to the minister. The head of the staff in that sense was directly answerable to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a summary of security-related events, incidents, and information of the MUP staff dated the 14th of March, 1999. We can see who the addressees were. Were you familiar with this summary, and what did it contain, if you received it?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: We used to receive such summaries from the ministry staff. Among others, I was one of the addressees, and I could see what the security related events, incidents, and information concerned was. It mostly dealt with terrorist attacks, their consequences, terrorist provocations, and committed serious crimes as well as traffic accidents and fires, explosions, which were particularly interesting for my sphere of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P701.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is tab 7 in your binder. We'll see a summary of security-related events, incidents, and information of the MUP staff dated the 25th of April, 1999. General, during the war in 1999, were you familiar with this summary sent by the MUP staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Formally speaking, I did not receive such summaries because they were not forwarded directly to me. However, I was always informed of them through the minister's cabinet. It differs slightly from the one we saw before because this one included NATO attacks. I was particularly interested in that because of the consequences following their bombings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see there information on certain people of Albanian and other ethnicities who fled from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English that would be page 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the NATO aggression against our country began, we were faced with the situation in which many Albanian citizens as well as Serbian citizens and other non-Serbs began leaving Kosovo and Metohija en masse. It was of great concern for us. We were able to verify that a large number of people were leaving the country, and the minister stated that first and foremost it came about as a result of the bombing and fear of being bombed, as well as fear of being caught in a clash between security forces and terrorists, as well as a result of propaganda activity undertaken in order to put up an image of a humanitarian disaster, as well as some threats levelled by terrorists forcing people to move out. Those were all reasons for people to move out of Kosovo, at least according to the information we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we are discussing information now, can you tell us how was information exchanged in the MUP of Serbia in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, we had guide-lines on informing and reporting within the Ministry of the Interior. It was clearly prescribed what urgent information was in terms of daily briefings, periodical briefings, et cetera. The intent was to have every last police station or OUP provide information to the competent Secretariat of the Interior, which in turn was under an obligation to provide such urgent information to the competent operational centre of the interior and to the staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, were people leaving the territory of the Republic of Serbia during the war even outside of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were people leaving the territory of Serbia, fleeing from the war, even those who were not in Kosovo and Metohija itself?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were many such cases. A lot of people left Serbia for neighbouring countries or further afield in fear of bombings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D407.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 8 in your binder. This is a daily review of current events and the occurrences relating to public security. The date in question is 22 April 1999. It was issued by the analyses administration of the Serbian MUP and its public security sector. The date of the document is 23 April, 1999. Can you tell us what sort of document is this?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: As we've already said, following the instructions on informing and reporting, the secretariats were under an obligation to forward all information as per list included in those instructions to the MUP staff and operational centre. The operational centre then forwarded such information to the analyses administration which compiled a summary of events and incidents for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia. Based on that, daily overviews were created in the field of public security and then such information was passed down to the MUP staff and the secretariats concerning all such security-related events of the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, sir, tell us this: Before Minister Stojiljkovic's staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija was established, did the Ministry of Interior have staffs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ever since the unfortunate events in Kosovo and Metohija in 1981 when a staff was formed by the Federal Ministry of the Interior, there existed such a staff. Units were sent to the staff from all of the former republics in the autonomous province of Vojvodina. It existed at the level the federal interior ministry until 1991 when a decision was issued on the setup of the staff of the public security sector. In that staff of the public security sector, there were only members of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D100.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which is tab 11 in your binder. Let me add this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, it's not tab 11, it's tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a decision on the formation of a staff of the ministry in Pristina. We'll see the name of the public security sector head, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. The date is the 15th of May, 1998. First of all, can you tell us what was the reason or the basis for the formation of this staff?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: It was based on Article 10 of the Rules on Internal Organisation of the Ministry of the Interior. In Article 10 of the rules, the public security sector chief is authorised to establish staffs, commissions, working bodies, and other Working Groups which may be tasked with dealing with different issues pertaining to the public security sector and the ministry. Under Article 2, as far as I recall, he was also duty-bound to inform the minister of the establishment of such a staff, or there had to have been a minister's order on such a staff to be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, tell us something about the tasks on page 1. In particular we have item 2. What were the tasks of the Ministry of Interior specified therein?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: All this falls within the remit of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move on to page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about the work of the staff and the situation with public security in terms of this decision and responsibilities assigned therein?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: For the work of the staff and the public security situation in the area of Kosovo and Metohija, it was the head of the staff who was answerable to the public security sector chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about item 6, what sort of information process was envisaged there?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Item 6 envisages that the head of the staff needs to inform the chief of the public security sector of the measures taken. I also wanted to add that the chief of the public security sector was under an obligation to inform the minister of this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P760.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 11, Witness. This is P706 [as interpreted], a decision on the composition of the staff, leaders, and members of the staff of the Ministry of the Interior for the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija dated the 11th of June, 1998, by General -- Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic, chief of sector and assistant minister. General, we can see here who the members of the staff were in item -- in chapter 1. As for the Roman numeral II, can you tell us who became a member of the expanded staff?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: The expanded staff also included chiefs of secretariats in the area of Kosovo and Metohija. They were also officials of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please go back to your tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to see P57. Page 3 in the B/C/S and 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, this is another decision on the setting up of staff for combatting terrorism issued by Mr. Stojiljkovic. What decision was made by the minister in item 6?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: In item 6, the minister decided that by virtue of that decision of the 16th of June, 1998, the preceding decisions on the formation of the staff of the ministry for the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija were rendered null and void. This was the only decision that remained in force following its issuance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, from October 1998 onwards, what was the security and political situation like in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, it was very, very complex. There was a constant threat of an aggression from the NATO pact. To that end, a number of measures and activities were undertaken in order for that moment to come, amid full preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up P356.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that's tab 12 with you, General. This is dispatch number 312 dated the 18th of February, 1999, from the sector chief, and that's the public security sector assistant minister Vlastimir Djordjevic. General, at the time the dispatch was made, were you aware of its contents?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was acquainted with the substance of the dispatch at the time it was made because I participated in its drafting, as did the chiefs of the affairs that I covered, i.e., all the chiefs of administrations; and subsequently assistant ministers as well took a look at the dispatch, and once they all agreed that it was properly made, it was forwarded to the sector chief who was in turn to hand it over to the minister. The minister approved the dispatch. It was signed and sent out into the field, or rather, I apologise, to the various organisational units of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the dispatch is addressed to?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: To all the organisational units of the public security sector in the headquarters, therefore, all the administrations and all the secretariats, the ministry staff in Pristina, border police stations, and the state security sector to the chief of the state security sector for his information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us why was this dispatch sent to the MUP staff for the prevention of terrorist activities in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, it was sent to the staff because it was a very important structure, in the field of the activities aimed at combatting terrorism. There was a threat of an aggression and they had to be made aware of one such dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And why was it sent to the RDB, for their information?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Wherever such a serious situation was involved as this one, which included defence from an aggression, we took care to send such dispatches to the state security sector for their information in order to keep them abreast of what it was that we were doing of the activities that we were engaged in since we were all part of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is it that the dispatch dictates?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see that it had to do with the defence from a potential aggression. In that context, we proposed a number of measures and activities to be undertaken in order for us to timely respond by taking measures and countering the consequences of a possible aggression. The dispatch was sent to all the secretariats and organisational units. If you want me to, I can speak to each and every one of these measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in the following: The measures that are proposed, do they distinguish between the secretariats located within Kosovo and Metohija and those located without?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: No. Since these were ordinary tasks falling within the remit of the public security sector, all the organisational units, regardless of the territory they covered, were sent such dispatches. In other words, no distinction was made as to the area of responsibility of a given secretariat. This was very important also to ensure uniformity of work and measures taken from the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see what the various tasks were within different fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to look at page 2, item 7. Can we have page 3 in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: General, as you read the text, can you comment on item 7, please.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: You see, we had intelligence to the effect that in the Republic of Serbia preparations were being made for possible establishment of paramilitary or para-police units. In that context, we instructed organisational units to take all operative measures and activities necessary in order to monitor such activities and counter them in order to prevent the establishment of paramilitary or volunteer units. This was the basic task. We had to be informed about their potential organising and arming to that, or rather, with the measures taken, we detected such groups in the making and we prevented them from being set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge from the war in 1999, were any paramilitary units active in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, there was no activity of paramilitary units in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, was there a specific reason why the chief of the public security sector himself issued this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: It was only natural for one such dispatch to be signed by the chief of the public security department since all the lines of work with the public security sector in the MUP were involved in its drafting, including assistant ministers. Therefore, it was only natural for the chief of the sector to sign one such dispatch and send it, of course, with prior approval of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which measures were taken by the headquarters of the Ministry of the Interior in the event of an aggression against the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MISIC
utterances.text: As far as the seat of the ministry is concerned, we developed plans for, among other things, its relocation to various locations, specifically of particular organisational units in the seat of the ministry, since the ministry itself is quite vast, organisation containing many different departments, we had to envisage their relocation. This also applied to the secretariats of the interior. They were given similar orders. Measures were also taken to raise the readiness overall of all the employees of the Ministry of the Interior. The locations where these various departments were envisaged to relocate had to be equipped with communication systems, et cetera.
